items.answer: A data analyst typically spends their day pulling data using SQL, cleaning and exploring it for patterns, building charts and dashboards, and writing up findings with recommendations. They also spend significant time clarifying questions and verifying data trustworthiness.

To become a frontend developer, core skills include HTML, CSS, and JavaScript, usually alongside TypeScript and a component framework like React. Important supporting skills are accessibility, responsive layout, calling HTTP APIs, version control with Git, browser developer tools, and component testing.

To get started in UX design, learn the fundamentals of usability and practise on real problems. You can pick an everyday app, test it with three people, and redesign one flow based on what you observed. Your portfolio should showcase your process and reasoning, including any changes made after testing, rather than just final screens.

A data analyst focuses on describing what has happened and why, using tools like SQL, descriptive statistics, and visualisation to help decision makers. A data scientist focuses more on prediction, experimentation, modelling, and uncertainty, using statistics and machine learning.

UX design focuses on how a product works, including the steps, structure, and task completion, appealing to those who enjoy research and problem framing. UI design focuses on the visual and interactive surface, such as layout, type, colour, and components, appealing to those who enjoy visual craft and detail. They overlap heavily, and a product designer does both.

A DevOps engineer builds and maintains the systems that transition software from a developer's machine to reliable operation in production. Their typical day-to-day work includes maintaining build and deployment pipelines, managing cloud infrastructure as code, setting up monitoring and alerts, responding to incidents, and automating repetitive manual work.

Core skills for a machine learning engineer include strong software engineering in Python, machine learning fundamentals, a deep learning framework, and model evaluation. Important supporting skills are data pipelines, deployment using containers and cloud services, monitoring, and prompt design, retrieval, and systematic evaluation for language-model applications.

To start as a backend developer, pick one language and build a small API with a real database to create, read, update, and delete records, then add login. Learn SQL properly without relying only on libraries. Deploy the project, add tests, and practise explaining your design choices.
QA engineers frequently transition into test automation engineering, backend development, DevOps, or product roles.

A product designer is responsible for a feature from the initial understanding of the problem all the way to the final interface, combining user experience design, user interface design, and an understanding of product and business needs.

To get started as a UX researcher, practise core methods on a small scale. Interview five people about how they perform a task, run a usability test on an existing app, and write a short report that separates observed facts from conclusions. An early key skill is learning to ask about past behaviour instead of opinions.
A data engineer builds the pipelines and storage that move data from where it is created to where analysts, data scientists, and applications can use it.

People who enjoy visual craft and detail such as typography, colour, and layout tend towards UI design. A UI designer focuses on the visual and interactive surface, including layout, typography, colour, components, and their states.

Frontend development focuses on interfaces, design detail, and accessibility. Backend development focuses on APIs, business logic, and data storage. Both require programming fundamentals, Git, and testing. Trying a small project of each kind is the most reliable way to find your preference.

Treat your assessment score as a starting point rather than a verdict. Use the topic breakdown to identify your weakest areas, review the explanations for missed questions, and select one or two topics to study before attempting the assessment again. Keep in mind that a higher score indicates related roles might align with your skills, though personal interest and practice are equally important.

A mobile developer needs to learn Kotlin for Android, Swift for iOS, or a cross-platform framework like Flutter or React Native. Important supporting skills include interface layout, state management, working with APIs, local storage, platform design guidelines, and debugging on real devices.
Site reliability engineering is a closely related role to DevOps engineering that focuses on keeping services available and fast.

A software tester, or QA engineer, designs test cases from requirements, conducts exploratory testing on new features, writes and maintains automated tests, reports bugs clearly with steps to reproduce them, and verifies that fixed bugs stay fixed.
You can move from a data analyst to a data scientist by adding programming in Python, deeper statistics, machine learning, and model evaluation.

To get started as a UI designer, study visual fundamentals and practise by rebuilding well-made interfaces to understand their spacing and type. Then, design a small set of components with all their states and use them to assemble a few screens, making sure to check contrast and keyboard focus from the beginning.
A data engineer builds the pipelines and storage that move data, and models tables in a data warehouse.
Data scientists design and analyse experiments such as A/B tests as part of their day-to-day work.
A UX design portfolio should show your process and reasoning, including what you changed after testing, rather than only displaying final screens.
A machine learning engineer increasingly builds applications on large language models with retrieval and evaluation.
Yes, SQL is a core skill for a data analyst and is used for pulling data.
Backend developers often grow into full-stack development, DevOps and site reliability work, or data engineering.

A backend developer should know one server-side language such as Java, Python, Go, or JavaScript. Additionally, they need to know relational databases and SQL, HTTP and API design, and data structures and algorithms.

A typical day for a UX designer involves talking to users, mapping user flows, sketching wireframes, building prototypes, and running usability tests. They then refine their designs based on what they learn from these activities and work closely with product managers and developers throughout the process.

To get started as a data engineer, you should become very good at SQL and comfortable in Python. Additionally, you can build a small pipeline that pulls data from a public API on a schedule, cleans it, loads it into a database, and checks its quality. Learning how to model tables for analysis is also just as important as learning tools.

Frontend developers often transition towards full-stack development by acquiring backend skills, or move toward design engineering and UI design by enhancing their visual and interaction skills. Mobile development is also a close neighbor that shares interface thinking.

A QA engineer, also known as a software tester, is responsible for finding problems before users encounter them and helping teams integrate quality into their processes. Their work includes planning tests, conducting manual testing, and writing automated tests.

To become a data scientist, you should build a base in statistics and probability, Python with data libraries, SQL, and machine learning methods together with honest model evaluation. Important supporting skills include experiment design, data visualisation, and communicating uncertainty clearly.

A UX designer focuses on how a product works for users by shaping task steps, organising information, mapping user flows, wireframing, and running usability tests. A product designer takes responsibility for a feature from the initial problem understanding to the final interface, combining UX design, UI design, and an understanding of product and business needs.

A UX researcher studies product users to help teams make evidence-based decisions rather than relying on assumptions. Their day-to-day work includes planning research with clear questions, recruiting participants, conducting interviews and usability tests, designing surveys, analyzing results, and presenting findings and their limits to teams.

Core skills for a DevOps engineer include Linux, networking fundamentals, scripting, continuous integration and delivery, containers, and at least one cloud platform. Important supporting skills include infrastructure as code, monitoring and logging, security basics, and calm, systematic troubleshooting.

To get started in mobile app development, you can choose one platform and build a simple complete app, such as a notes or expense tracker that saves data on the device. Next, add a network call and handle the case where the network is unavailable. Publishing even a small app will teach you the full release process.
Data engineers often transition into analytics engineering, machine learning engineering, or data platform and architecture roles.

A UI designer works on designing screens and components, defining styles for type, colour and spacing, specifying states such as hover, focus, error and loading, maintaining a design system, and working with developers to ensure the built result matches the design.
